proposal_status: The core idea is sound and needed. It is not approved as written: four parts are unsafe or cannot be met with the data we have (see required_constraints C1, C2, C5, C8). The narrowed version in minimum_interface is approvable.
source_findings: rh_qedushat_hayom (readings.json:8065), Hebrew segments 9-17 (lines 8209-8338): segment 9 is the only one with corresp=urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/melokh_al_kol_haolam. No segment has end_reference. The P milestone stays open until close_references() runs at the end of the unit, so the whole-root scope is really built by build.py's 'if paragraph is not None: close_references()'.

Old segment 14 '(מלכנו)' has no condition, no marked flag, and keeps its parentheses. It carries editorial_note, which build.py neither renders nor puts in unit_review_text. Old segment 13 ends 'וּדְבָרְךָ' and segment 15 starts 'אֱמֶת'.

musaf_malkhuyot_close (readings.json:47915) has the same scope shape. Segment 0 has corresp=.../musaf/malkhuyot_close/text, every segment has source=P, and only the last segment has end_reference. So the new source needs a mapping that does not close the frame just as much as the old one does. canonical_words is needed for the new source too, not only for the old one.

The new source splits the opening at a page break: segment 0 (s208) ends 'וְיֹאמַר' and segment 1 (s210) starts 'כֹּל'. The English splits the same way (s209 'created it' / s211 'and that every form'). The old source has each language's opening as one fragment (segment 9). One-segment-to-one-target mapping therefore cannot share an 'opening' part between the two sources. Either the parts are cut at the new page break, so the old segment 9 needs 2 targets attested by the new segments 0 and 1, or the new segments 0 and 1 stay unmapped.

The two printings differ in wording, not only in whitespace: פְעַלְתּוֹ (old) vs פְּעַלְתּוֹ (new), בְּאַפּוֹ vs בְאַפּוֹ, לְעָבְדְּךָ vs לְעָבְדְךָ, and 'מָשָׁלָה' vs 'מָשָׁלָה: '. Whitespace-normalised equality will fail unless each difference is an explicit wording overlay.

English, old and new: one segment, 'and purify ... who sanctifies', covers both Hebrew parts on either side of Malkeinu. Neither source prints English A and B separately. A multi-target mapping for English would need a split invented by the editor. That is exactly the 'substring inference' the proposal forbids.

The baseline does NOT protect the documentary frame: SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS already includes corresp, source and reference_unit, and snapshot() removes them. Under the current baseline, deleting segment 9's corresp=P or the new source's source=P would pass silently.

minimum_interface.field: segment['canonical_words']: a non-empty list of strings. Phase 1 requires exactly 1 item. Phase 2 (multi-target) is allowed only under C8.
minimum_interface.baseline.py: Add 'canonical_words' to SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS. The existing accepted hashes do not change because the field is absent today. Add a separate frozen frame fixture; do not edit marmorstein_accepted_660.json.
realizations.py: CANONICAL_WORDS_SEGMENT_KEYS = {'paragraph','fragments','corresp','reference_unit','source','end_reference','canonical_words'} | {'conditions','marked','condition_instruction','condition_instruction_language','speaker'}. speaker_before_reference is excluded (see C2). source_reference, source_reference_corresp, chapter_corresp, source_reference_part, source_reference_end, end_reference_before_instructions, editorial_note, repeat, transclude, repeat_cue, anchor, edition_label, deferred_page_boundary, condition_end_corresp, canonical and canonical_end are all excluded.
words_text(readings, lang, targets, settings): join_source_fragments over [canonical_text(t) for t in targets], resolving each target only as a pure-part identity.
marked_projection(segment): if marked is true, strip exactly one outer '(' ... ')' from the single fragment and fail otherwise. With no marked flag the text is returned unchanged.
validate_word_mapping(readings, stem, mapping): a new redirect preflight in baseline.py, separate from validate_redirection.
minimum_interface.build.unit_document: In the per-fragment branch, after the existing pb, conditional, reference milestone and speaker handling, and where literal words would go: emit one <j:transclude type='inline' target=t+'@'+project/> per target, into the existing content node (the <seg source> if present, else the paragraph). Never call close_references(). Keep the existing separator logic: add a space unless join_next. Do not add canonical_words to the condition that rewrites pb/@ed to '1965 <context>'; the pb ed/n/facs values of the old file must stay byte-identical.
minimum_interface.build.build identity loop: Add canonical_words targets to the registry/alias check alongside canonical and canonical_end.

required_constraints: C1 Protect the frame: for every segment that has canonical_words, every key other than canonical_words must equal a frozen accepted frame record. This covers corresp, source, reference_unit, end_reference, conditions and marked. The same applies to every other segment of that unit/language, and to unit-level urn, map_root and title. The baseline cannot do this because it removes corresp and source. Use a new fixture, in the same style as marmorstein_qedushah_before_reuse.json, for rh_qedushat_hayom and musaf_malkhuyot_close.

C2 Never close scopes: reject speaker_before_reference on canonical_words segments, because build.py closes active_reference when it is set. Reject biblical corresp, source with reference_unit='verse' plus a bible source, and any chapter-opening path: each of these calls close_references() and would cut the enclosing P scope. Reject edition_label, which also closes references.

C3 Exclusivity: a segment cannot have both canonical and canonical_words, nor canonical_end. A unit with canonical_whole, canonical_home, text_corresp or canonical_parts, or with reuse in that language, cannot contain canonical_words. canonical_home's context pass removes corresp and would destroy the frame.

C4 Targets: each target must be in pure_ids (a segment identity of a canonical_parts unit). Reject the following: library roots (pure_roots); ranges (split_range, or '-' forms); '@' qualifiers; the segment's own corresp or any identity open at that point, including P itself; any root identity; duplicates within one list; and cycles. Cycles are impossible if libraries stay free of transcludes, but assert that anyway.

C5 Exactly one plain fragment: fragments must have length 1, keys within PLAIN_FRAGMENT_KEYS, and no prepare_unit overlay on the caller (no alternatives or optional_spans). Compare ' '.join(words_text.split()) with ' '.join(marked_projection(segment).split()) exactly. The only projection is the marked-parenthesis strip.

C6 Library attestation: in the pure-part attestation loop, a library fragment is attested only by (a) an existing single canonical pointer with no canonical_end, or (b) a single-target canonical_words segment whose marked_projection text, scan and printed_page equal the library fragment exactly. A multi-target segment never counts as an attestation.

C7 Integration: extend every place that currently only looks at segment['canonical'] so it also covers canonical_words. That means attesting_controls (covered set), review_payloads (trigger plus one fidelity entry per segment holding targets[], projection, settings and enclosing_scopes), validate_occurrences (used_features for wording_selection, fidelity) and validate_generated (identities set, so each library part is checked for exactly one home).

C8 Multi-target (phase 2 only): allowed only if every target in the list also has its own independent single-target attestation in another unit. Under that rule the old Hebrew/English opening could be backed by the new segments 0 and 1. The English 'and purify ... who sanctifies' A+B case stays unmapped and documentary. Not allowed together with marked. Each target's corrected and resolved hashes are recorded separately.

C9 Pointing differences: every difference between the printings is a wording_variants overlay on the library, with registered condition URNs and the library's printed reading first, selected by the caller's wording_selection. Whitespace normalisation must never absorb pointing or punctuation.

C10 Whole-root safety: while P's host contains canonical_words, reject any canonical, canonical_end, canonical_whole, reuse, repeat, transclude, citation, repeat_cue or order reference whose target is P (or a range touching P). Reason: _range_segments(P) returns only segment 9, not the milestone scope, and canonical_text would now reject segment 9 anyway. This gap already exists today; this change makes it reachable.

C11 Corrections: canonical_corrections.py is not in the bundle, so this was not verified. bind_corrections attesters must either include canonical_words segments, or corrections on canonical_words targets must be rejected until they are bound.

C12 No other ways round it: no contextual-controls library mode, no relaxing of canonical_text or validate_pure_parts, no repeat/transclude path to pure parts, and source is never substituted for corresp.
risks: Cutting canonical parts at a page break of the new printing ('וְיֹאמַר | כֹּל') bakes a print artifact into canonical identity. The alternative is to leave the new segments 0 and 1 unmapped and attest 'opening' from the old segment 9 alone (single target).
Encoding dagesh and colon differences as opensiddur:variant overlays creates choices users can see in the expanded spine, and validate_generated will add caller defaults for them.
The English expanded spine will be missing 'and purify ... who sanctifies' unless C8 is relaxed by inventing a split. Do not relax it silently; make it an explicit editorial decision.

Exporter behaviour was not verified: whether an inline transclude inside a prayer-part milestone range is expanded when P is resolved, whether library P/part milestones are copied into P's output, and whether URN-hierarchy resolution sends P/part to P's document.

Paths I tried: /tmp/mahzor-s254/processor/schema, /tmp/mahzor-s254/processor-worktree/schema, /tmp/mahzor-s254/worktree/schema, /tmp/processor/schema. Whether j:transclude is valid inside tei:seg[@source] (every new-source segment gets one) still needs checking.
editorial_note is silently dropped today and is not in the review payload. That is unchanged by this proposal, but mapped segments must not hide it further.
better_existing_interface: None covers the case. canonical closes references, canonical_home rejects segment conditions and removes corresp, canonical_whole needs a plain single paragraph, and pure-part ranges are forbidden. canonical_words is the minimal addition. The fallback, which needs no code, is to leave the old Melokh segments literal under P, so the whole-root stays intact and there is no duplicate identity, and to use canonical_words only where a 1:1 attested alignment exists. Use that fallback for the English A+B segment and for whichever source's opening loses the granularity choice.
required_tests: Actual-source generation for both units in he and en: the old P milestone exists exactly once, and find_end_of_mapping from it ends at the original boundary (after segment 17). Exporter resolution of P under shabbat=unknown/true/false yields the full old recitation, including the literal '(מלכנו)' and its documentary conditions.

Every library part has exactly one generated home. The old and new files contain only j:transclude for parts, never corresp=P/part. No library milestone, pb, note or conditional appears in the expanded P output.
pb n, facs and ed and their text positions are identical before and after, in both old and new files. unit_review_text and the snapshot are unchanged. All 660 baseline hashes still pass.
Frame fixture: mutating corresp, source, reference_unit, end_reference, conditions or marked on any segment of the mapped unit fails, even though the baseline would allow it.

Rejections: speaker_before_reference, biblical corresp, source_reference/chapter_corresp/source_reference_part, editorial_note, alternatives/optional_spans on the caller fragment, 2 fragments, canonical plus canonical_words, canonical_home/canonical_whole/reuse units, root/library-root/range/'@'/self/open-ancestor/duplicate targets, malformed conditions, condition_instruction without conditions, unknown speaker role.

Marked cases: '(X)' with marked strips exactly one pair; without marked the parentheses stay; unbalanced or missing parentheses with marked fail; old '(מלכנו)' (unmarked) cannot attest a part 'מלכנו'.
Wording: wrong pointing (פְעַלְתּוֹ/פְּעַלְתּוֹ) or a missing colon fails without an overlay and passes with a registered overlay plus selection. Unused or partial selection fails.

Receipts: changing a library word, an overlay, the caller's conditions or marked flag, another attester's conditions, an enclosing scope, the target list or order, or a correction changes every affected realization/<stem>/<lang> payload. Reordering units does not.
Phase 2 only: multi-target with a sole attestation is rejected (English A+B); multi-target backed by independent single-target attesters passes; marked plus multi-target is rejected.
Pointers to P while its host has canonical_words are rejected: canonical, reuse, repeat, transclude, citation, repeat_cue, expanded_order or source_order reference.
Schema validation of a generated file with a transclude inside seg[@source] and inside j:conditional[@type='marked'].
